note: The lead set work to null on 2026-10-31: the Education Act bans only school-hours work and no text read says Nauru sets no minimum age, which is silence, as New Zealand's is held. Nauru, read on RONLAW (ronlaw.gov.nr, the Republic's online laws, service 6 of 2026), 2026-10-31. Majority: the Interpretation Act 2011, s. 2 (service 4): an adult is an individual who is at least 18, and a child one who isn't; no other Act setting full age or a minor's contractual capacity was found among the 437 Acts RONLAW lists, so majority is held as 18 (my reading). Work: no Act sets a minimum age for employment: RONLAW's Acts include no employment standards law beyond the Workers (Contracts of Service) Act 1922 (which sets none that was found); the Education Act 2011, s. 17, bars employing a school-age child (4 to 17 on 1 January) during school hours, and the Child Protection and Welfare Act 2016, s. 53, makes the employer of a child prove the child's age when asked and, where a law permits employing someone under 18, obtain a parent's consent (neither held). So, as with New Zealand's file, from is 0 and performers are free, held only by the school-hours rule (my reading; a law not on RONLAW, or a later Act, would change it). Service: Nauru has no armed forces and no Act on RONLAW deals with military service, so service is none (a reading from absence).
